timeline: You need to know how 110 million gallons of water drowned 375 miners during the Chasnala disaster on December 27, 1975.
Miners warned the coal barrier was thin.
Miners blamed management negligence over safety as an abandoned flooded mine lay right above.
Management ignored warnings and blasted the seam.
At one thirty-five, the barrier ruptured.
Seven million gallons flooded every single minute.
The colliery lacked high pressure rescue pumps.
Numbered helmet lamps identified the recovered bodies.
The mine lacked adequate safety equipment, requiring high-pressure pumps to be brought in from the Soviet Union and Poland.
Recovered bodies were typically identifiable only by the number on their lamp helmets.
